questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
She wanted us to start the semester by (pushing / pushed) ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves.

det.ref:
[원문] She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones.
[해석] 그녀는 우리가 안전지대를 벗어남으로써 학기를 시작하기를 원했다. [문장 03 참고]
det.correct: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 합니다. pushed(과거분사)는 전치사의 목적어가 될 수 없습니다.
wrongs: ① pushing ✅ — 전치사 by + 동명사(V-ing) 구조
② pushed ❌ — 과거분사는 전치사 목적어 불가
det.tip:
💡 전치사 + 동명사
• by/in/of/about/for + V-ing
• 예: by studying hard

⚠️ 함정
• 전치사 뒤 to부정사 불가
• 단, look forward to V-ing에서 to는 전치사

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
The important part was (trying / to try) something new for each one.

det.ref:
[원문] The important part was trying something new for each one.
[해석] 중요한 부분은 각각의 도전에서 새로운 것을 시도하는 것이었다. [문장 06 참고]
det.correct: 보어로 동명사 trying이 적절합니다. 주어 The important part의 보어로 동적 의미를 전달합니다.
wrongs: ① trying ✅ — 보어로 동명사 적절
② to try ❌ — 문맥상 동명사가 더 자연스러움
det.tip:
💡 동명사 보어
• 주어가 동명사이면 보어도 동명사: Seeing is believing

questions.passage: To help us do so, she gave us an ( ___ ) to challenge ourselves in three different ways.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 10자, a로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways.
[해석] 그녀는 세 가지 다른 방법으로 도전하라는 과제를 주었다. [문장 04 참고]
det.correct: assignment = 과제, 임무 (=task, homework)
det.tip:
💡 어휘
• assignment: 과제, 임무
• 동의어: task, homework, duty

questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. ( ___ ), if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 7자, H로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, ...
[해석] 요즘 나는 스트리밍으로 영화를 보는 편이다. 하지만 극장에 가면, ... [문장 08~09 참고]
det.correct: 스트리밍 시청 습관 ↔ 극장 방문: 대조 관계이므로 역접 연결사 However가 적절합니다.
det.tip:
💡 역접 연결사
• However: 접속부사 (문장 앞, 쉼표)
• But: 등위접속사 (문장 중간)

questions.passage: However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. <u>Those</u> are the kinds of movies <u>they</u> enjoy.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 Those와 they가 각각 가리키는 것으로 올바른 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy.
[해석] 그것들은 그들(친구·가족)이 즐기는 종류의 영화이다. [문장 10 참고]
det.correct: 앞 문장에서 "an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family"가 언급되었으므로, Those는 그런 영화 장르를, they는 friends or family를 가리킵니다.
wrongs: ① ✅ — Those=액션·SF영화, they=친구와 가족
② ❌ — Those는 영화 장르, 스트리밍 서비스가 아님
③ ❌ — 역사 드라마는 나중에 혼자 볼 때 선택한 것
④ ❌ — they는 선생님과 학생들이 아닌 친구·가족
⑤ ❌ — Those는 도전 과제가 아닌 영화 종류
det.tip:
💡 지칭 추론
• 대명사는 직전 문장이나 같은 문장에서 선행사 찾기
• Those = 복수형 지시대명사 (앞에 나온 복수 명사 가리킴)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Going to the theater alone (was / were) something I had never done before.

det.ref:
[원문] Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before.
[해석] 혼자 극장에 가는 것은 내가 전에 한 번도 해본 적 없는 것이었다. [문장 11 참고]
det.correct: 동명사구 "Going to the theater alone"이 주어이며, 동명사 주어는 단수 취급합니다.
wrongs: ① was ✅ — 동명사 주어 = 단수
② were ❌ — 동명사 주어에 복수 동사 불가
det.tip:
💡 동명사 주어의 수일치
• 동명사(V-ing) 주어 → 항상 단수 동사
• 예: Swimming is good exercise.

questions.passage: So, for the first challenge, I decided to <u>give it a try</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 give it a try의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] I decided to give it a try.
[해석] 나는 그것을 시도해 보기로 결심했다. [문장 12 참고]
det.correct: "give it a try" = "try it / attempt it" = 시도해 보다
wrongs: ① ❌ — give up의 의미
② ✅ — try it, attempt it
③ ❌ — give in의 의미
④ ❌ — return, give back의 의미
⑤ ❌ — give a chance의 의미
det.tip:
💡 give 관용 표현
• give it a try = 시도하다
• give up = 포기하다
• give in = 양보하다, 굴복하다

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I chose a historical drama (that / what) I had been curious about.

det.ref:
[원문] I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about.
[해석] 나는 궁금해했던 역사 드라마를 골랐다. [문장 15 참고]
det.correct: 선행사 a historical drama가 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 적절. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 선행사가 있으면 사용 불가.
wrongs: ① that ✅ — 선행사(a historical drama) 있음 → that
② what ❌ — what은 선행사 포함(=the thing that), 선행사와 함께 사용 불가
det.tip:
💡 that vs what
• that: 선행사 있음 → the book that I read
• what: 선행사 포함 → I read what I liked

⚠️ 선행사가 있으면 what 사용 불가!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
But once the movie started, I became completely (absorbing / absorbed) in the story.

det.ref:
[원문] I became completely absorbed in the story.
[해석] 나는 이야기에 완전히 몰입했다. [문장 17 참고]
det.correct: 주어 I(사람)가 감정을 느끼는 대상 → 과거분사 absorbed. absorbing은 감정을 유발하는 것에 사용.
wrongs: ① absorbing ❌ — 감정 유발 주체(사물)에 사용
② absorbed ✅ — 감정을 느끼는 주체(사람)에 사용
det.tip:
💡 감정 분사
• V-ing: 감정 유발 (The movie is absorbing.)
• p.p.: 감정 경험 (I was absorbed.)
• 빈출: interested/interesting, bored/boring

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
It was so (satisfying / satisfied) just to focus on the movie itself.

det.ref:
[원문] It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself.
[해석] 영화 자체에 집중하는 것은 매우 만족스러웠다. [문장 18 참고]
det.correct: 가주어 It = to focus on the movie itself(진주어). 진주어가 만족감의 원인이므로 현재분사 satisfying이 적절.
wrongs: ① satisfying ✅ — 진주어(to focus)가 만족감 유발 → V-ing
② satisfied ❌ — 가주어 It이 사람이 아니므로 satisfied 부적절
det.tip:
💡 가주어 It 구문의 분사
• It(가주어) = to V(진주어, 감정 원인) → 현재분사(-ing)

⚠️ 함정
• It을 사람으로 착각하여 satisfied를 고르는 실수 주의!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
This experience made me (realize / to realize) that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone.

det.ref:
[원문] This experience made me realize that ...
[해석] 이 경험은 내가 ... 깨닫게 했다. [문장 20 참고]
det.correct: 사역동사 make + O(me) + 동사원형(realize). to realize는 사역동사 make 능동형에 불가.
wrongs: ① realize ✅ — make + O + V원형
② to realize ❌ — make 능동형에서 to 불가 (수동: be made to V)
det.tip:
💡 사역동사 make
• 능동: make + O + V원형
• 수동: be made + to V (to 부활!)

⚠️ let + O + V원형 / have + O + V원형

questions.passage: I didn't have to worry about anyone else's ( ___ ).
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 11자, p로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences.
[해석] 다른 사람의 선호를 걱정할 필요가 없었다. [문장 14 참고]
det.correct: preferences = 선호, 기호 (=tastes, inclinations)
det.tip:
💡 어휘
• preference: 선호 (prefer의 명사형)
• 동의어: taste, inclination, liking

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 모두 찾아 바르게 고친 것은?
At first, it felt a bit ⓐawkwardly and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story. It was so ⓑsatisfied just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me ⓒto realize that I sometimes enjoy ⓓto do things alone.

det.ref: [원문] 문장 16~20 참고
det.correct: ⓐ felt(감각동사)+형용사 → awkward, ⓑ It(가주어)=to focus(감정 원인)→satisfying, ⓒ make+O+V원형→realize, ⓓ enjoy+V-ing→doing
wrongs: ① ✅ — 4개 모두 올바르게 수정
② ❌ — satisfied는 사람 주어에 사용, 여기서는 satisfying
③ ❌ — awkwardly와 to realize가 수정되지 않음
④ ❌ — to do가 수정되지 않음
⑤ ❌ — to realize가 수정되지 않음
det.tip:
💡 핵심 4가지 규칙
• 감각동사 + 형용사 (부사 X)
• 가주어 It(감정 원인) → V-ing
• make + O + V원형
• enjoy + V-ing (동명사만 목적어)

ch: ③ ⓐ awkwardly ⓑ satisfying ⓒ to realize ⓓ doing
④ ⓐ awkward ⓑ satisfying ⓒ realize ⓓ to do
⑤ ⓐ awkward ⓑ satisfying ⓒ to realize ⓓ doing

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid (of / for) water.

det.ref:
[원문] I've always been afraid of water.
[해석] 나는 항상 물을 무서워해 왔다. [문장 22 참고]
det.correct: be afraid of ~: "~을 두려워하다"의 고정 표현.
wrongs: ① of ✅ — be afraid of + 명사
② for ❌ — be afraid for는 "~를 걱정하다" (다른 의미)
det.tip:
💡 afraid 전치사
• be afraid of + 명사: ~을 두려워하다
• be afraid to V: ~하기를 두려워하다
• be afraid for + 사람: ~를 걱정하다

questions.passage: For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. ( ___ ), I wasn't sure what to do at first.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 7자, H로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] However, I wasn't sure what to do at first.
[해석] 하지만 처음에는 뭘 해야 할지 몰랐다. [문장 25 참고]
det.correct: "극복하기로 결심" ↔ "뭘 해야 할지 모름": 대조 관계 → However
det.tip:
💡 역접 연결사
• However = 하지만 (접속부사, 문장 앞 + 쉼표)
• Nevertheless = 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I came across a video clip of my cousin (surfing / to surf) at an indoor pool on social media.

det.ref:
[원문] I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool.
[해석] 실내 수영장에서 서핑하는 사촌의 동영상을 우연히 보았다. [문장 26 참고]
det.correct: "my cousin surfing"은 명사 + 현재분사 구조. 서핑하고 있는 사촌의 영상.
wrongs: ① surfing ✅ — 현재분사가 명사(cousin) 후치수식
② to surf ❌ — to부정사는 목적이나 의도를 나타내어 부자연스러움
det.tip:
💡 명사 + 현재분사 (후치수식)
• a video of my cousin surfing = who was surfing
• 현재분사: 능동/진행의 의미로 명사 수식

questions.passage: One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. <u>It</u> looked fun, and I liked the fact that <u>it</u> took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 두 It/it이 각각 가리키는 것으로 올바른 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean.
[해석] 그것은 재미있어 보였고, 바다가 아닌 얕은 수영장에서 한다는 사실이 좋았다. [문장 27 참고]
det.correct: 첫 번째 It은 앞 문장의 video clip(영상)을 가리키고, 두 번째 it은 서핑 활동을 가리킵니다.
wrongs: ① ✅ — It=영상, it=서핑 활동
② ❌ — 첫째 It은 사촌이 아닌 영상
③ ❌ — SNS나 수영장이 아님
④ ❌ — 실내 수영장이 "재미있어 보였다"는 부자연스러움
⑤ ❌ — 둘째 it은 바다가 아님
det.tip:
💡 대명사 추론
• it은 직전 문장의 명사 또는 상황을 가리킴
• "took place"(일어났다) → 활동/행사를 가리킴

ch: ① 첫째 It=영상 / 둘째 it=실내 서핑 활동
④ 첫째 It=실내 수영장 / 둘째 it=사촌의 서핑

questions.passage: She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I [sign] up for a beginner course.
questions.stem: [sign]을 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오. (1단어, 영문 6자, s로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] so I signed up for a beginner course.
[해석] 그래서 나는 초급 과정에 등록했다. [문장 29 참고]
det.correct: 과거 시제 문맥이므로 sign → signed
det.tip:
💡 sign up for
• sign up for: ~에 등록하다
• 과거형: signed (규칙 변화)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I learned how (balancing / to balance) properly and even managed to surf a few waves!

det.ref:
[원문] I learned how to balance properly.
[해석] 나는 제대로 균형 잡는 방법을 배웠다. [문장 31 참고]
det.correct: 「의문사 + to부정사」 구문: how to V = ~하는 방법
wrongs: ① balancing ❌ — how balancing은 문법적으로 성립하지 않음
② to balance ✅ — how to V = ~하는 방법
det.tip:
💡 의문사 + to부정사
• how to V / what to V / where to V
• learn/know/decide + 의문사 + to V

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
"물속에 있는 것은 내가 생각했던 것만큼 나쁘지 않았다."

det.ref: [원문] Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. [문장 33 참고]
det.correct: ① 동명사 주어(Being) + wasn't as ~ as + 과거완료(had thought)가 모두 올바름.
wrongs: ① ✅ — 동명사 주어 + not as~as + 과거완료
② ❌ — so bad as는 부정문에서 가능하나, thought의 시제 오류
③ ❌ — 동명사 주어는 단수 → weren't 불가
④ ❌ — 구조 변경 + think 시제 불일치
⑤ ❌ — isn't(현재) + have thought(현재완료) → 시제 불일치
det.tip:
💡 원급비교 부정
• not as(so) + 원급 + as
• 과거완료: 과거보다 더 이전 시점의 행위

ch: ① Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought.
② To be in the water wasn't so bad as I thought.
③ Being in the water weren't as bad as I had thought.
④ It wasn't as bad to be in the water as I think.
⑤ Being in the water isn't as bad as I have thought.

questions.passage: ( ___ ) the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 5자, W로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.
[해석] 그 경험이 생각을 완전히 바꾸진 못했지만, 모험심을 발견하게 해주었다. [문장 34 참고]

questions.passage:
"To grow into a better version of ourselves, we should not stay as we are." That was the first thing our teacher said to us on the first day of school. She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our relationships. The important part was trying something new for each one. She told us that we should share our experiences with our classmates when we finished the challenges.

These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about. At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story. It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.

Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.

Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to draw attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited me. The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about myself.

I learned a lot about myself through this assignment, and I found out that my classmates did, too. One of them tried new foods from different countries, while another joined a creative writing club. Through these experiences, we all realized how important it is to push ourselves to try new things. We gained different perspectives on life and had a lot of fun, too! My classmates and I even talked about setting more challenges for ourselves. There are always more things that we can discover about ourselves, and it's exciting to keep learning and growing. We never know what we're capable of until we try!

wrongs: ① ❌ — 혼자 영화 보기는 도전 중 하나일 뿐
② ✅ — 안전지대 벗어나기의 이점
③ ❌ — 수상 스포츠가 최선이라는 내용 없음
④ ❌ — 외모 변화→인기 연결 없음
⑤ ❌ — 안전지대 머무름의 위험은 다루지 않음
